question.text: Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function \[ f(x) = \begin{cases}\dfrac{2}{15} (6-x), \quad &2 \leq x \leq 5\\[5pt] 0, \quad &\textrm{otherwise}\end{cases} \] its cumulative distribution function is \[ F(x) = \begin{cases} 0, \quad & x < 2 \\[5pt] h(x), \quad & 2 \leq x \leq 5\\[5pt] 1, \quad & x > 5. \end{cases} \] Find the function $h(x).$
question.explanation:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that is strictly positive only for $2 \leq x \leq 5,$ the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

\[ F(x) = P(X \leq x) = \begin{cases} 0, & x < 2 \\[5pt] \displaystyle \int_2^x f(t) \, \textrm dt, & 2 \leq x \leq 5 \\[5pt] 1, & x > 5 \end{cases} \]

For the given probability density function, we have

\[ \begin{align*} \int_{2}^x f(t) \, \textrm dt &= \int_{2}^x \dfrac{2}{15}(6-t) \, \textrm dt \\[5pt]\ &= \left. -\dfrac{1}{15}t\left(t-12 \right) \right|_{2}^x \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{1}{15}x( x - 12)-\dfrac43 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{-x^2 +12x-20}{15}. \end{align*} \]

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

\[ F(x) = \begin{cases} 0, & x < 2 \\[5pt] \bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue} \dfrac{-x^2 +12x-20}{15}}, & 2 \leq x \leq 5 \\[5pt] 1, & x > 5. \end{cases} \]

example.title: Finding a CDF Given a PDF With Lower and Upper Bounds

question.text: Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function \[ f(x) = \dfrac{e^{-\left|2x/3\right|}}{3}, \quad x \in (-\infty, \infty), \] its cumulative distribution function is \[ F(x) = \begin{cases} h(x), \quad & x < 0 \\[5pt] 1-\dfrac{e^{-2x/3}}{2}, \quad & x \geq 0. \end{cases} \] Find the function $h(x).$
question.explanation:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that involves an absolute value, the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

\[ F(x) = P(X \leq x) = \begin{cases} \displaystyle \int_{-\infty}^x \dfrac{e^{2t/3}}{3} \, \textrm dt, & x < 0 \\[5pt] \displaystyle \int_{-\infty}^0 \dfrac{e^{2t/3}}{3} \, \textrm dt + \int_{0}^x \dfrac{e^{-2t/3}}{3} \, \textrm dt, & x \geq 0 \end{cases} \]

Let's compute the integrals.

  • If $x \leq 0,$ we have \[ \begin{align*} \int_{-\infty}^x \dfrac{e^{2t/3}}{3} \, \textrm dt &= \left. \dfrac{e^{2t/3}}{2} \right|_{-\infty}^x \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{e^{2x/3}}{2}, \end{align*} \] Therefore, \[ \begin{align*} \int_{-\infty}^0 \dfrac{e^{2t/3}}{3} \, \textrm dt &= \left. \dfrac{e^{2x/3}}{2} \right|_{x=0} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}. \end{align*} \]

  • If $x > 0,$ we have \[ \begin{align*} \int_{0}^x \dfrac{e^{-2t/3}}{3} \, \textrm dt &= -\left. \dfrac{e^{-2t/3}}{2} \right|_{0}^x \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{e^{-2x/3}}{2} + \dfrac12. \end{align*} \] As a result, we get \[ \begin{align*} \int_{-\infty}^0 \dfrac{e^{-2t/3}}{3} \, \textrm dt + \int_{0}^x \dfrac{e^{-2t/3}}{3} \, \textrm dt &= \dfrac{1}{2} + \left( -\dfrac{e^{-2x/3}}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} \right) \\[5pt] &= 1-\dfrac{e^{-2x/3}}{2}. \end{align*} \]

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

\[ F(x) = \begin{cases} \bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue} \dfrac{e^{2x/3}}{2}} , & x < 0 \\[5pt] 1-\dfrac{e^{-2x/3}}{2}, & x \geq 0. \end{cases} \]

example.title: Computing a CDF Given a PDF That’s Nonzero Over All Real Numbers

question.text:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the cumulative distribution function \[ F(x) = \begin{cases} 0, & x < 0 \\[5pt] \dfrac{x^2}{144}, & 0 \leq x \leq 12 \\[5pt] 1, & x > 12, \end{cases} \]

find $P(4\lt X \leq 6).$
question.explanation:
We can perform this computation as follows:

\[ \begin{align*} P(4\lt X \leq 6) &= P(X \leq 6)-P(X\leq 4) \\[3pt] &= F(6)-F(4) \\[3pt] &=\dfrac{6^2}{144}-\dfrac{4^2}{144}\\[3pt] &= \dfrac{5}{36} \end{align*} \]

example.title: Computing a Probability Over an Interval Using a CDF

question.text:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the cumulative distribution function \[ F(x) = \begin{cases} 0, & x < 4 \\[5pt] 1 - \dfrac{16}{x^2} , & x \geq 4, \end{cases} \]

find $P(X > 6).$
question.explanation:
The cumulative distribution function of a continuous random variable $X$ is the function $F(x)$ defined by

\[ F(x) = P(X \leq x). \]

Hence, the required probability is

\[\begin{align} P(X > 6)&=1-P(X \leq 6)\\[5pt] &=1-F(6)\\[5pt] &=1-\left(1 - \dfrac{16}{6^2}\right)\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{4}{9}. \end{align} \]

example.title: Computing a Probability Over an Interval Using a CDF

question.text:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function \[ f(x) = \dfrac{4e^{2x}}{(1+e^{2x})^3}, \quad x \in (-\infty, \infty), \]

find the cumulative distribution function $F(x).$
question.explanation:
The cumulative distribution function of a continuous random variable $X$ is the function $F(x)$ defined by

\[ F(x) = P(X \leq x) = \int_{-\infty}^x f(t) \, \textrm dt. \]

For the given probability density function, we have

\[ \begin{align*} F(x) &= \int_{-\infty}^x f(t) \, \textrm dt \\[5pt] &= \int_{-\infty}^x \dfrac{4e^{2t}}{(1+e^{2t})^3} \, \textrm dt \\[5pt] &= \left. - \dfrac{1}{(1+e^{2t})^2} \right|_{-\infty}^x \\[5pt] &= - \dfrac{1}{(1+e^{2x})^2} + 1 \\[5pt] &= 1 - \dfrac{1}{(1+e^{2x})^2}. \end{align*} \]
